findings.where: Motion sketch, the 'Replay the entrance' control (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: This is a button that replays the animation on the spot. It is styled exactly like the page's links: blue with an underline, like the email address and the PDF link. On this page, one look therefore means two different things. Where the link look appears, it should always mean 'this takes you somewhere'.
findings.who_objects: The founder testing the tile, and later anyone carrying this link style into the built site. Blue with an underline promises that clicking leads somewhere, but here it reruns an animation in place. Once the style becomes a shared component, the ambiguity spreads to every page.

findings.where: Article specimen, the 'Download' entry 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge'
findings.fault: The entry looks like a working download link, and its metadata line says 'PDF'. But the parts map shows the link goes to '#', so clicking it jumps back to the top of the page instead of opening a document. The brief names the PDF list as part of the product, so this is a dead action on an item the visitor is told to download.
findings.who_objects: The founder reviewing the tile, and the bank or agency reader it stands in for. Expecting the lecture PDF, they are thrown back to the top of the page with no sign of what happened.
